statement: In the exact-rank-three heavy-null normal form A=RBR^T with s_min(B)>=1, heavy row sqrt(c)e1, 1/2<c<1, and normalized residual frame (w,v,uhat) satisfying w_j^2+v_j^2+uhat_j^2<=1/2, one has ||p_Q||inf <= 9.6 |det B|^(-1/3)[c(1-c)]^(-1/6) <= 9.6[c(1-c)]^(-1/6). The density in this positive-leak branch is continuous C0. For c<=127/128 the bound is <24.191.
exact_structural_identities: Residual coefficient vectors satisfy ||u||^2=1-c, ||w||=||v||=1 and u,w,v are pairwise orthogonal.
After scaling Q_* = Q/(beta sqrt(c)), the transverse cross magnitude is epsilon=sqrt((1-c)/c) and the square coefficient is lambda=gamma/(beta sqrt(c)).
The density scale collapses exactly to |det B|^(-1/3)[c(1-c)]^(-1/6).

premises.scope: arbitrary hub law; light orthonormal (w,v,qhat) frame; density <=9.6(eps|lambda|)^(-1/3); characteristic function O(|t|^-3/2)
TW J(tau)<=K(1+|tau|) suffices for uniform light-frame hub/twist closure

designated_partner_result_applied.actual_application: At c=1 Parseval forces u=0, so the frame is support-separated; with s_min(B)>=1 the partner theorem gives ||p_Q||inf<248.

narrowed_survivor: Under the normalized light-frame hypothesis it is enough, after r28 and this run, to treat 127/128<c<1, overlap Gram kappa>1/2, with total longitudinal leak ||u||^2=1-c<1/128. The exact c=1 endpoint is paid by the partner theorem.
unresolved_implication: QFORM-TINY-LEAK-ENDPOINT-STABILITY-v1: obtain a bound uniform as epsilon=sqrt((1-c)/c)->0+ in the product-linear light-frame hub/twist core, equivalently pay the named TW estimate or a coarea substitute with the same endpoint stability.
continuity: proved in the positive-leak spread subbranch by integrable O(|t|^-3/2) Fourier decay; full-target continuity remains open
